reference.title: Dumbbell Lying Extension (across face)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the dumbbell lowers beside the head, exhale as you straighten the arm.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.4 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: More reps, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet planted. Hold one dumbbell straight up over the shoulder, neutral grip (palm facing in, handle along your body); rest the other hand on your stomach.
Keep the upper arm still and breathe in as you bend the elbow, lowering the dumbbell across above your face toward the opposite shoulder.
Forearm across above the chin, dumbbell over the opposite shoulder with the palm facing your face, elbow pointing up; keep it clear of the face.
Breathe out and straighten the elbow along the same path.
Arm straight, squeeze the triceps, repeat; then switch arms.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arm drifting across the body
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow pointing straight up over the shoulder; only the forearm crosses.
Keep both shoulder blades on the bench; brace lightly.

mistakes.mistake: Lowering onto the face or chin
mistakes.fix: Stop with the forearm across above the face; the dumbbell stays over the opposite shoulder, not on you.
Straighten the elbow without snapping it.

kinematics.norm: From straight to about 90-100 degrees, stopping before the dumbbell reaches the head (clinical opinion)
Over the shoulder, here tilted slightly toward the head so the forearm crosses above the face, and still (clinical opinion)
Neutral at the top (palm toward the midline); the palm ends facing the face, the handle staying along the body so neither end points at you (clinical opinion)
The upper arm is turned in so the forearm swings across the body instead of back toward the head; the dumbbell passes above the face to over the opposite shoulder (clinical opinion)
Rests on the stomach; some lifters steady the working upper arm with it instead (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020 (head, shoulders and hips on the bench)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual Dumbbell Lying Extension (across face), video page (movement reference; page not readable here)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

Maeo and Kanehisa, triceps hypertrophy after 12 weeks of elbow extension training with the shoulder at 180 versus 0 degrees of flexion (Descente Sports Science vol 41; full paper: Maeo et al. 2023, Eur J Sport Sci 23(7):1240-1250, PubMed 35819335)

Solstad, Andersen, Shaw, Hoel, Vonheim and Saeterbakken 2020, a comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males (J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651; PMC7675616)

cautions: The dumbbell travels over the face: use a light, fixed-plate dumbbell and a slow, controlled lowering.
Elbow pain: shorten the range and use a lighter dumbbell (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrist straight over the forearm; a bent-back wrist under the dumbbell strains it.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: let the upper arm tilt slightly toward the head.
Elbow discomfort: lighter dumbbell, shorter range.
regressions: Two-arm lying extension with light dumbbells.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Only mover: straightens the elbow while the upper arm stays vertical. Long and lateral head activity differed in lying barbell triceps extensions (Boehler 2011); the long head works at a longer length the higher the arm is raised (Maeo and Kanehisa). Turning the upper arm in moves the bend across the body; the elbow still does all the work (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handle and hold the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm vertical as the dumbbell lowers behind the elbow.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still on the bench.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Holds the upper arm turned in so the forearm stays on the cross-body path (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Forearm swings across, upper arm still
Elbow a little past 90 at the bottom
